All coherent. The remaining `fast-forward` references are in unrelated functions (`_sync_branch`, `_reconcile_registered_worktree_to_origin`); the covering-point region and function name are consistent. Change scope is exactly my three locked files plus the loop's own pre-existing `.shiki` bookkeeping.

The implementation is complete and verified. Here is the summary.

## Result
- **Goal/task:** G-20260806T065143407702Z-8e3284ce / T-20260806T065143409817Z-dbdae1cf — "Stage every coordinator mirror write, not only the three sync paths" (amended: **commit**, not stage)
- **Role:** Implementer
- **Status:** ready (for the loop to deliver — commit/push/PR/merge are loop-owned)

## What changed or decided
The previous implementation **staged** the coordinator's `.shiki` mirror at the single covering point in `execute_action`'s `finally`. Measurement showed staging clears only a **fast-forward** `git merge origin/main`; the coordinator always carries its own commits, so its merge is always **non-fast-forward**, where a merely-staged returning file still aborts (*"Your local changes … would be overwritten by merge"*). Fix in `scripts/shiki_loop.py`:

- `_stage_coordinator_mirror` → **`_commit_coordinator_mirror`**: `git add --ignore-removal -- .shiki`, then a **plain index commit** (`git commit --no-verify`, only when the add staged something) — never `git commit -- .shiki` (which re-reads the tree and would record a deletion, breaking the append-only mirror).
- Kept every prior property: ONE covering point every effector passes through; scoped to `.shiki`; `--ignore-removal` so no deletion is ever staged.
- **Removed** the prior contract's unmeasured non-goal ("the local branch must not advance") — the coordinator branch is disposable and never pushed/merged, so advancing HEAD costs nothing. That non-goal was exactly what made staging unable to satisfy its own criterion.
- A genuinely-differing file yields a normal `CONFLICT (add/add)` for the operator — documented in the docstring, **not** auto-resolved (no merge driver/strategy).
- Updated two stale comments that still said "fast-forward"/"staging only".

## Checklist status
- **Skill Gate:** `tdd` (tests changed to assert committing → RED against staging code → GREEN after the change), `code-review` (independent adversarial review — no blocking findings; two non-blocking items both addressed)
- **TDD:** every merge assertion rebuilt to be **divergent (non-FF)** — the old tests passed vacuously fast-forward. Added `test_covering_point_never_deletes_a_mirror_record` (tracked record survives) and `test_genuinely_differing_file_conflicts_normally_not_a_refusal`; made the second merge assertion in `CoordinatorStagingAfterSyncTests` divergent too.
- **CCA/MergeGate:** owned by the loop on delivery.

## Evidence
- `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` → **1091 OK**
- `bash scripts/test_shiki_goal_loop.sh` → passed (its real multi-cycle `loop run` now commits per effector)
- `python3 scripts/validate_shiki.py --target .` → passed (exit 0)
- Independent reviewer verdict: nothing blocking; confirmed tests non-vacuous (real tracked record for the no-delete test; every merge asserted divergent before it runs)
- **Files changed (all in locks):** `scripts/shiki_loop.py`, `tests/test_closeout.py`, `tests/test_dispatch_state_sync.py` (the `.shiki/{goals,locks,tasks}` entries in `git status` are the loop's own pre-existing bookkeeping, present at session start, untouched by me)

## Next action
- The Shiki loop owns commit → push → PR (with the MergeGate body) → merge. Note for CCA/operator: this design **advances the coordinator HEAD** by construction and, on a genuine divergence, surfaces a normal `add/add` conflict for manual resolution — both are intended and documented in `_commit_coordinator_mirror`.
